selector.rationale: The presence of progressive, multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques, along with milia in the superficial dermis, supports Epidermolysis Bullosa Pruriginosa. The genetic variant in COL7A1 also aligns with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, but the lack of extracutaneous involvement and specific mention of pruriginosa features makes Epidermolysis Bullosa Pruriginosa a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lichen Planus

rejected.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: The genetic findings and clinical presentation do not align well with junctional epidermolysis bullosa, which typically involves more severe and early-onset skin blistering.
